title: Design Engineer
tagline: Live where design and code meet: interfaces, motion and design systems.
about: Design engineers (also called UX engineers or UI engineers) bridge designers and developers. You prototype in code, build design systems, craft interactions and animations, and make sure the shipped product feels as good as the mockups.
It's a great fit if you care about details: spacing, motion, typography, the half-second that makes something feel delightful.
day: Prototype interactions in code to test ideas fast
Translate Figma designs into pixel-perfect, accessible UI

phases.title: Design fundamentals
phases.goal: See like a designer: layout, type, colour and hierarchy.

nodes.d: Hierarchy, alignment, contrast, repetition and white space: why some screens feel calm and others chaotic.
Choosing, pairing and setting type so it's readable and expressive.
Palettes, contrast and colour in dark mode.
The industry's design tool: frames, auto layout, components and variables.
User research, flows and usability testing.

project.d: Pick an app you use, redesign one screen in Figma with a clear rationale, then write up before/after.

phases.title: Front-end craft
phases.goal: Build interfaces that match the design exactly and work for everyone.

nodes.d: Layout, custom properties, container queries, :has() and cascade layers.
links: CSS-Tricks: A complete guide to CSS Grid

nodes.d: Enough programming to build real interactive components.
Composable, accessible components with clean APIs.
Keyboard patterns, screen readers and ARIA authoring practices.
Crisp vector graphics you can style and animate.

phases.title: Motion & interaction
phases.goal: Make interfaces feel alive without making them slow or dizzying.

nodes.d: Easing, timing and choreography: motion that explains rather than decorates.
Transitions, keyframes, the Web Animations API and spring physics.
Native animated transitions between states and pages.
Generative visuals and 3D on the web.
60fps animations: animate transform and opacity, avoid layout thrash.

project.d: A gallery of five polished micro-interactions (toggle, drag-to-reorder, toast stack, command palette, shared-element transition), each accessible and respecting reduced motion.

phases.title: Design systems
phases.goal: Scale design across teams and products.

nodes.d: Colours, spacing, type and radii as data, synced between Figma and code.
Build, document and version a component library.
Shared language, handoff, critique and prototyping to settle debates.

project.d: Tokens, ten documented components in Storybook, light/dark themes, accessibility tests and a demo app built only from them.

interview: Portfolio walkthrough: explain decisions, not just visuals.
Build a component live from a design with keyboard support.
Critique an existing interface and propose improvements.
